newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-RECOVERING SCHULTZ RATES SOUTH AFRICAN PACE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-RECOVERING SCHULTZ RATES SOUTH AFRICAN PACE.

text.p: South African fast bowler Brett Schultz has backed the Proteas' four-man pace attack to win the opening test against India.

The left-armer, currently fighting his way back to full fitness after breaking a bone in his heel during South Africa A's tour of England this year, has been showing signs of returning to his fastest and most aggressive for Western Province in the last few weeks.

His name is already being mentioned as a possible candidate for the series against Australia which immediately follows India, but he has much ground to make up as a string of others have leap-frogged over him in the queue to make the test team.

On Thursday, Schultz, who made his test debut against the Indians in 1992, will see South Africa line up with the experienced pair of Allan Donald and Brian McMillan joined by the fit-again Shaun Pollock and rookie Lance Klusener, both of whom will be playing on their home pitch.

"I think we'll see Javagal Srinath with a smile on his face when he sees the pace and bounce in the Kingsmead pitch, but then I think there's another four seamers for South Africa with even bigger smiles," Schultz said.
In the recent series in India which the home side won 2-1, South Africa were hampered badly by the fact that Pollock was unable to make the tour at all and Donald picked up an injury halfway through.

Their return will naturally strengthen the team and the Indians will also be haunted by bad memories of their last series in 1992, which South Africa won 1-0, when a number of batsmen appeared to be genuinely scared of the Donald-Schultz combination.

However, the South African batsmen will also have to be wary of the India's less pacy but wily duo of Srinath and Venkatesh Prasad although Schultz has reservations about Prasad's effectiveness outside India.
"I'd like to see him on South African wickets which are more suited towards seamers.
"He bowled well with variation of pace in India but, here in South Africa, variation of pace is not as effective as it is in India. I really fancy South Africa's chances of victory in Durban."
Schultz's most recent injury is just one in a long list which has restricted him to just seven tests in nearly five years.
He has had operations on both his knees and suffered the embarrassment of hobbling out of his last test appearance against England at Centurion Park last year with a strained buttock muscle.
